pairs.subject: draft-editing
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/MandateEditor.tsx:268 Exiting the editor via the back button invokes onClose without checking dirty state or intercepting navigation, causing uncommitted in-memory draft changes to be dropped upon unmount.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/owner/diff.ts:93 Dirtiness is dynamically derived per-term and per-clause by comparing baseline to draft over canonical values rather than storing mutable dirty flags.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/owner/SignSheet.tsx:53 Applying the draft submits the full payload to mandate_sign rather than diffs, and mutations bypass a unified patch door via direct spreads.
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/owner/data.ts:12 Debouncing is only utilized for read-only what-if simulations, with no autosaving or debounced save groups persisting draft data.
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/MandateEditor.tsx:268 The back button exits the surface unconditionally without a navigation guard, discard confirmation, or remount persistence.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/mandateDraft.ts:92 Magic defaults such as 6 rounds and 1-day deadlines carry no documented rationale or incident history, and bounds are not clamped at a patch door.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/MandateEditor.tsx:370 Incomplete drafts cannot be saved freely because no intermediate draft persistence exists distinct from the disabled promotion signing control.

pairs.registryProposal: The draft-editing standard assumes web-style continuous background autosaving (debounced-save-groups), but high-security local client applications with cryptographic signing workflows intentionally avoid intermediate persistence of unsigned drafts to prevent unencrypted/unauthenticated state from lingering at rest.
